operations_plan.summary: Create and insert a separate, parameterized mounting screw into the left base through-hole without modifying the existing bracket geometry.

steps.description: Identify the first mounting location from the cylindrical wall of the left base mounting through-hole, face 1. Retrieve its cylindrical axis, center, and measured diameter of 15 mm. Retrieve the upper seating plane from face 57 and the table-facing underside from face 59; their Y locations indicate a 15 mm base thickness. Define the insertion direction from the exposed upper face toward the underside as -Y. Do not use the top actuator bore or transverse pin bore as mounting references.

Create a new fastener component rather than adding material to solid 0. Use a standard screw whose shank has running clearance in the measured 15 mm hole; if a catalog standard must be selected without further input, use a generic M14 screw as the provisional choice. Keep the screw diameter, thread pitch, under-head length, head type, and material parameterized because these specifications were not supplied. Set the under-head length to at least the 15 mm plate thickness plus a configurable protrusion for engagement with a threaded table hole or nut.

Model or instantiate the first screw with its longitudinal axis normal to the base upper seating face. Create the cylindrical shank concentrically about the axis obtained from face 1 and extend it in -Y through the full base thickness and below face 59 by the configurable table-engagement allowance. If detailed threads are required, apply the selected external thread only to the intended engagement portion; otherwise use a cosmetic thread or simplified cylindrical shank to avoid inventing an unsupported pitch.

Create or configure a conventional accessible screw head above face 57. Use a generic socket-head form unless a project fastener standard is available. Make the head diameter larger than the 15 mm through-hole while keeping it inside the local end pad of the rounded base plate. Add the catalog under-head fillet, top edge treatment, drive recess, and shank-tip chamfer when available. Do not countersink or counterbore the existing base hole because such modifications were not requested.

Apply assembly relationships to the first screw: constrain the screw axis concentric with cylindrical hole face 1, constrain the underside of the screw head coincident with upper seating face 57, and orient the shank toward face 59 along -Y. Retain the screw as a separate component and verify that it does not intersect the cylindrical hole wall or the rounded outer boundary of the base pad.

operations_plan.summary: Create a matching second screw from the first fastener definition and insert it into the opposite base mounting through-hole.

steps.description: Identify the second mounting location from cylindrical face 0, the right base mounting through-hole. Retrieve its axis and center directly from the cylindrical geometry and confirm that its measured diameter and Y-directed axis match face 1. Use the same upper seating face 57, underside face 59, screw standard, and configurable under-head length established for the first mounting screw.

Create a second instance of the first screw component so both mounting fasteners have identical shank diameter, head geometry, thread definition, material, and under-head length. Keep it as a separate assembly occurrence with planned solid identifier new_solid_right_mounting_screw; do not fuse either screw to bracket solid 0.

Place the second screw by constraining its axis concentric with cylindrical hole face 0. Constrain the underside of its head coincident with upper seating face 57 and orient its shank along -Y through the plate toward and beyond underside face 59. Confirm that both heads are visible and accessible from the upper side of the base and that both shanks project toward the table-facing side.

Validate the completed assembly. Confirm one screw is concentric with face 1 and one with face 0, both heads seat on face 57, and neither screw interferes with the base-hole walls or surrounding rounded end pads. Preserve the existing 15 mm hole diameters, hole centers, spacing, axes, base thickness, and all upright C-frame, jaw, recess, yoke, pin-bore, and actuator-boss geometry. Because the table is not modeled, leave the below-base engagement length configurable and do not create table holes, nuts, washers, countersinks, or base modifications unless separately specified.
